title: March Comes in Like a Lion
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: Rei Kiriyama lost his parents and sister in an accident, grew up as the resented foster son of a shogi master, and now lives alone as a 17-year-old professional shogi player. The warm Kawamoto sisters, Akari, Hinata and Momo, draw him slowly out of isolation as he grows both as a player and as a person.
life_message: It holds up a life of patient effort and of letting others in, where chosen family and honest work heal loneliness.

content.note: Very little; conflict is played out over the shogi board (Wikipedia plot).
Grief for dead family members and heavy loneliness (Wikipedia; MediaBleach death-of-parent and grief warnings).
Foster sister Kyoko is in love with Goto, a married man (Wikipedia characters); nothing explicit noted (to verify).
Some insults and harsh words from Kyoko and the bullies (to verify).
Older rivals get Rei drunk and abandon him; Akari works evenings as a bar hostess (Wikipedia).
Rei's depression and a long arc of Hinata being bullied at school (Wikipedia reception; MediaBleach; MangaUpdates Bullying).
Rei leaves home and school early, later chooses to return to high school (Wikipedia).

dominant: Communitarianism (found family), Existentialism, Classical virtue ethics

delivery.note: Healing through chosen family is carried by Rei's growth; cruel characters are shown as wounded, per the entry summary.

winners_losers: Patient, caring people such as the Kawamoto sisters and the striving Rei earn sympathy; bullies and the cruel, manipulative Kyoko are shown as wounded rather than simply defeated. A humane, communal worldview gets the story's sympathy.
